summary: Read the one-line AGENTS example and all three complete SolidSL lesson sidecars. Preserve their symbolic shape controls, exact-versus-marched distinction and generated GLSL demonstration. Hoist field lowering out of the dense sampler, teach the existing native scope, and qualify what the comparison actually measures.

lenses.smells_idioms: No raw box properties or box aliases. refusals rebuilds the field closure tree inside each parallel level-set evaluation; SolidField.kt toLevelSetField calls recursive toField3. Both longer native examples close only on success even though Solid.scope and AutoCloseable.use already exist.
lenses.imports: Retain afield.lang.solidsl.* pending deterministic resolution; SolidSL is absent from Boxes.kt intro. MeshView and mesh extensions are in intro but their mechanical disposition belongs to the analyzer. ManifoldLibrary is outside intro. No star-import removal proposed and no analyzer report supplied.
lenses.whitespace: The long run blocks in cross_check and refusals are flush with their outer code, obscuring the lexical scope and return@run. Indent those block bodies mechanically while retaining the shape declaration groups and labelled data pairs. Do not split the authored shape tree into arbitrary fragments.
lenses.comments: Shape controls and the faceting explanation are useful. cross_check calls a vertex-sampled deviation an everywhere bound; use sampled wording. The volume/triangle-count stability demonstration is useful evidence but the existing SolidBuild.isExact is the direct source of exact-path truth.
lenses.glsl: glsl_backend contains calls that emit GLSL, rather than authored shader bodies. Preserve toGlsl/toRaymarchFragment and the comments on scalar SSA and step scale; inspect the real emitted fragment in later verification rather than reformatting Kotlin strings as GLSL.
lenses.live_coding: No fragment markers or declaration/assignment reset pairs occur. boreRadius, slotWidth, quality, twist, blend and fillet are easy to find. Native scope closure is especially useful for repeated full runs; geometry stays as a reusable immutable expression value.
lenses.helpers: Checked the helper register including all declined proposals. Reuse existing Solid.scope, SolidBuild.use and a captured Field3; no new level-set wrapper required. Formatting helpers x.f3 are already approved follow-ups, not a fresh proposal. Existing SolidBuild.isExact and SolidAgreement.kind should carry exactness claims.

findings.issue: This callback lowers the entire expression on every grid sample. SolidField.kt:83 constructs toField3(), whose recursive implementation begins at line 195. That places repeated closure-tree allocation on the dense parallel evaluation path and lengthens feedback after editing fillet.
findings.proposed_change: Compute val field = part.toLevelSetField() once before Solid.levelSet and pass field = field::at, as the existing API KDoc shows.
findings.verification: Compare sampled values/topology before and after; replay the hybrid/naive comparison and inspect viewer output.

findings.issue: build and naive own native handles but their close calls occur only at the end. An exception during levelSet, mesh conversion or display bypasses both. cross_check similarly closes coarse/fine/exact only on the success path. Solid has a Cleaner, so the issue is delayed and nondeterministic release during iterative runs, not a proven permanent leak.
findings.proposed_change: Use the existing Solid.scope around the native demonstration, with a Unit result, or nested use blocks. Keep extracted TriMeshes as the display payload; avoid returning a Solid from the scope when it should close. Apply the same ownership convention to cross_check.
findings.verification: Run successfully and with a deliberate exception in a disposable session; verify handles close on both paths and viewers still draw copied mesh data.

summary: Read all six full Faust bodies and the transcript setup/replay context. Keep the independent offline render path, one-oscillator chord proof, silent-gap check and explicit steal control. Correct two measurement explanations that currently overstate what the reported values establish.

lenses.smells_idioms: The live instrument returns inst as its final value, preserving FaustPolyLaunch ownership and its feeder/bank close path. Offline faustPatternRender owns a separate bank and closes it in finally; no Runloop sampler is introduced. No raw properties, box aliases or renderer lookups occur.
lenses.imports: All six bodies explicitly import afield.audio.synth.*, a package already in the box intro. Preserve it until the deterministic analyzer makes a resolved decision; no analyzer report was supplied. Fully qualified WavFloatArrayWriter remains an API helper opportunity rather than an unsupported import rewrite.
lenses.whitespace: Preserve Faust control alignment, triple-quoted program bodies, the top-level steal control and multi-line note/automation arguments. Long result-print chains can be split into named measured values when fixing the measurement wording; do not hide DSP setup in a new abstraction.
lenses.comments: Most comments explain useful reasons: poly controls by label, sustain gaps, spectral isolation and distinct output channels. Timing prints sample-exact unconditionally and only scans from the expected frame, so it cannot detect early attacks. The steal explanation confuses a ratio of normalized steps with the raw normalized step.
lenses.glsl: Not applicable: embedded source is Faust DSP, not GLSL. Keep the #faust headers, Faust signal routing and control row alignment. A GLSL formatter must not touch those strings.
lenses.live_coding: No authored fragment markers or declaration/assignment reset pairs exist. The steal knob explicitly requests a full rerun and should remain near the top; changing an offline render does not need mutation of the running audio graph. Keep inst as the live body final expression.
lenses.helpers: Checked Already in Field, Approved and Declined sections. showFaustPattern already renders and displays, but it recompiles/rerenders and cannot simply display a previously measured FaustPatternRender. A small WAV conversion member/extension could remove four repeated engine-level calls; this is a new proposal for human review. x.f3 is already approved and must not be re-proposed.

findings.issue: The search begins at the expected frame n and only looks forward. An attack that started early also has mono[n] != 0 and gets counted exact. Neither preceding silence nor per-note gap correspondence is checked, and line 212 prints sample-exact regardless of exact/checkable. This is a measurement limitation established by reading the loop, not a claim that the scheduler currently runs early.
findings.proposed_change: Keep the transparent measurement, but require a verified silent interval before each measured onset and locate the zero-to-nonzero transition within a bounded window spanning both sides of n. Print sample-exact only when every eligible onset agrees; otherwise report signed error or an inconclusive gap condition.
findings.verification: Replay the real default render, then use deliberately advanced/delayed render buffers and a no-gap sustain variant to verify the measurement does not falsely report sample-exact.

findings.snippet: println("A ratio near 1.0 means the biggest one-sample jump is as big as the whole local peak —")
findings.issue: stealRatio divides faustNormalisedStep at the steal by faustNormalisedStep in a settled window. A ratio near 1 means those normalized steps are similar, not that either step equals the local peak. The explanatory sentence belongs to the numerator statistic documented in FaustPattern.kt, and reverses the interpretation of the printed comparison.
findings.proposed_change: Explain ratio near 1 as no extra normalized jump relative to the settled baseline; print the numerator separately if discussing a jump as large as its local peak. Keep stealReleaseFrames and the two explicit audio comparisons.
findings.verification: Render 1-frame and 1440-frame releases, record numerator/denominator/ratio and confirm the text describes the actual figures; inspect and listen to both real outputs.

findings.issue: The already-rendered result is repeatedly unpacked into the same engine-level stereo WAV encoder: two chord calls, timing, and each steal comparison. This is presentation ceremony around a result that already knows its channels and sample rate.
findings.proposed_change: Consider a FaustPatternRender.wav(normalizePeak = 0.9f) conversion using the existing encoder, then keep explicit display channel names. Do not rerender through showFaustPattern or add an audio device dependency.
findings.verification: If approved later, compare encoded WAV bytes and metadata against the existing four call sites and inspect the real players.
